Developed by Indian startups under the IndiaAI Innovation Centre, the models aim to advance the vision of making AI in India and for India using subsidised national compute infrastructure.

stories.title: Karnataka hosts 51 percent of India's global capability centres
stories.summary: Karnataka now hosts 1,088 of India's 2,117 global capability centres, according to state minister Priyank Kharge. The state also accounts for 43 percent of the country's AI and machine learning talent within these centres. The findings were released at the Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026.

stories.title: Wadhwani AI and LinkedIn partner to train Northeast SMEs
stories.summary: Wadhwani AI and LinkedIn have launched a 12-month programme to train 2,000 small entrepreneurs in Northeast India on AI applications. The initiative focuses on digital skills for marketing and operations across sectors including handloom, food processing, and tourism. Practical training will cover generative AI for social media.

stories.summary: Anthropic closed its Nasdaq debut at $97.17, a 17% increase from its $83 IPO price. Investors remain hungry for exposure to the boom.

stories.summary: Anthropic has raised $81.3 billion in the largest initial public offering in history, reaching a valuation of approximately $1.5 trillion. The San Francisco-based developer priced 980 million shares at $83 each, exceeding its initial range due to investor demand. It has surpassed the previous record set by SpaceX.

stories.title: Anthropic stock opens at $111.50 after record $81.3 billion offering
stories.summary: Anthropic shares opened at $111.50 on Thursday, surging 34% above the $83 offering price. The Nasdaq debut briefly pushed the company's valuation to $2 trillion before shares retreated toward $100. The listing serves as a test of investor confidence in the artificial intelligence market.

stories.title: Anthropic offers discounts to gain ground with new products
stories.summary: Anthropic is offering credits of up to $2,000 per user and discounts exceeding 30% to encourage companies to adopt its new products. The firm is pushing tools like Claude Code and Claude Cowork to match the rapid growth of its AI business functions.

Anthropic value rises above $2 trillion in stock market offering
stories.summary: Anthropic launched on the Nasdaq on Thursday, with its value briefly exceeding $2 trillion. The company's IPO prospectus included a 94-page health warning, noting that its products could help terrorists develop biological weapons or trigger the extinction of the human race. It is the largest public offering ever.

stories.title: France passes data transmission tax by one vote
stories.summary: France approved a new levy charging internet companies 0.055 euros for every gigabyte of data delivered to users. The measure passed the National Assembly by a single vote, 11 to 10. The tax affects companies running large-scale internet and artificial intelligence services in the country.

stories.title: Claude maker Anthropic pops in Nasdaq debut
stories.summary: Anthropic shares soared 34% to open at $111.50 following an $81.3 billion IPO. The stock peaked at $115.10, briefly valuing the company at more than $2 trillion on a fully diluted basis, before paring gains as the broader market slid.

stories.title: AI helps researchers investigate how thousands of medical studies share code
stories.summary: Researchers are using AI to examine the methods and choices behind medical studies. Scientists note that the way data is prepared and models are developed, often called researcher degrees of freedom, significantly affects the results and reproducibility of scientific work.

stories.title: Survey of eighty-eight studies reveals severe shortage in Amharic
stories.summary: A review of 88 studies published between 2015 and 2024 found that 98% failed to investigate conversational AI for Amharic. Despite global breakthroughs in large language models, the development of systems tailored to the language spoken by over 30 million people remains largely unaddressed.

stories.title: Open weight AI improves biomedical reproducibility but requires complete access
stories.summary: A study in Annals of Biomedical Engineering reports that many biomedical studies using large language models cannot be reproduced. Researchers cite reporting limitations and the challenge of accessing proprietary models, noting that third-party providers can alter or withdraw systems at any time.

stories.title: Orthopedic artificial intelligence shifts focus toward external validation
stories.summary: A narrative review in Knee Surgery and Related Research finds a persistent divide between technical AI development and clinical translation in orthopedics. While publication growth is exponential, adoption remains constrained by performance degradation, algorithmic opacity, and a lack of external validation in clinical settings.

stories.title: Synthetic clinical data approached real records in bilingual medical study
stories.summary: Researchers found that synthetic clinical records generated by an instruction-tuned model performed similarly to real data on diagnostic coding tasks. The study aimed to address privacy regulations that restrict access to genuine clinical narratives like radiology reports and discharge summaries.

stories.summary: MIT researchers estimate that data center electricity demand caused 650 premature deaths in 2023. While power usage is concentrated in Virginia and Texas, the resulting air pollution impacts regions far from the facilities. Some Midwestern states recorded the highest per capita rates of premature deaths from the electricity load.

stories.title: ChatGPT rated more reliable than Gemini and Copilot for dental queries
stories.summary: Researchers compared AI platforms on their ability to answer layperson orthodontic questions. ChatGPT provided more accurate and reliable responses than Google Gemini or Microsoft Copilot regarding retainers and implants. Large language models are increasingly used as medical information sources, despite varying levels of factual dependability across different platforms.

stories.title: Texas A&M researchers develop AI for cellular disease modeling
stories.summary: Researchers are building AI virtual cell technology to predict how genetic changes and drugs alter cellular behavior. The project aims to explain why diseases occur and how to design treatments, addressing current limitations in AI models that can predict disease development but lack insight into biological mechanisms and interventions.

stories.title: Vectorial AI raises $3 million to simulate consumer behavior
stories.summary: Vectorial AI has secured $3 million in seed funding to expand its SAPIENS model, which simulates audience behavior to streamline consumer research. The company, founded in 2024, aims to address software development bottlenecks as AI tools move from pilot programs into production environments.

stories.title: Nvidia stock drops following earnings call
stories.summary: Nvidia stock is trading at approximately $150 per share, a 40 percent decline from its October 6th peak. The drop follows the company's third quarter earnings call and reports regarding executive leadership. Meanwhile, Anthropic debuted on the Nasdaq at a price 34 percent higher than analysts had expected.

stories.title: Data center expansion faces political and public pushback
stories.summary: Voters largely opposed data center expansion during the 2026 midterms, citing concerns over power grids and utility bills. While tech giants promise to work with local communities, Democratic leaders are calling for further restrictions and slowdowns on the construction of energy-hungry server warehouses.

stories.title: Global data center power demand projected to double by 2030
stories.summary: The IEA reports that global data center power demand will double by 2030, requiring $4 trillion in spending. The build-out of 93 large AI factories is expected to add 50 gigawatts of capacity, straining electricity grids that are already struggling to support current peak loads.

stories.title: Oak Ridge National Laboratory advances AI factory plans
stories.summary: Oak Ridge has opened its 4,032-GPU Lux system for scientific users. The facility is now attracting proposals for nuclear generation and uranium projects to support future data center needs. The Department of Energy is seeking private development on federal land, though no specific developers have been selected.

stories.title: Nvidia reports doubling of quarterly revenue
stories.summary: Nvidia announced third quarter revenue of $115.8 billion, a 103 percent increase year-over-year. The company attributed the growth to sustained demand for AI and data center infrastructure, with data center revenue alone rising 110 percent. Gross margins for the period reached 74.8 percent.

stories.title: Airsys introduces thermal management for data centers
stories.summary: Airsys has launched Arc90, a thermal management architecture that combines air and liquid cooling. The system utilizes a Power Compute Effectiveness metric to measure efficiency. The company intends to use the framework to change how it scopes and prices projects by treating cooling as an integrated design outcome.

stories.title: Core Scientific advances Oklahoma data center project
stories.summary: Core Scientific is developing a 100-megawatt data center in Muskogee, Oklahoma, to support AI workloads. The facility is part of a 500-megawatt hosting agreement with CoreWeave. Approximately 70 megawatts of the site's capacity will be dedicated to critical IT equipment for NVIDIA GPU infrastructure.

stories.title: Data center power market expected to exceed $42 billion
stories.summary: Dell'Oro Group forecasts the high-density power market for data centers will top $42 billion by 2030. The growth is driven by the transition of AI racks from 50V to 400V and 800V architectures to manage increasing power requirements.

stories.title: Sophia Space deploys edge computing in orbit
stories.summary: Sophia Space has deployed its orbital operating system on Kepler satellites, marking a first for constellation-scale edge computing. The system runs on 40 NVIDIA Jetson Orin modules. The company describes the deployment as a step-by-step approach to building space infrastructure rather than launching a traditional data center.

stories.title: Intel reports 70 percent yield on 18A process
stories.summary: Intel announced that yields for its 1.8nm-class 18A manufacturing process have reached 70 percent. Microsoft has signed a long-term agreement to use Intel's Xeon supply and EMIB packaging technology, becoming the first company to publicly commit to the new fabrication process.

stories.title: Ubisoft launches AI studio amid reorganization
stories.summary: Ubisoft has established Motherbrain, a standalone subsidiary dedicated to developing generative AI for video games. The studio will focus on creating new gameplay mechanics and interactive possibilities. The launch is part of a wider company reorganization that began in January 2026.

stories.title: Managers mandate AI as employees use it by choice
stories.summary: Slingshot surveyed 500 U.S. employees and managers, finding a gap between mandated AI adoption and actual workplace utility. While managers increasingly require AI tools, most employees report using them by choice. The study suggests employers should measure verified output time rather than counting prompts or adoption rates.

stories.title: Open-weight AI models shift governance to employers
stories.summary: Open-weight models allow companies to run AI on their own systems, offering cost savings alongside full accountability. A federal lawsuit involving Meta employees highlights the legal risks of using AI for workforce decisions. When companies deploy AI to manage personnel, they own the resulting consequences.

stories.title: Psychotherapist reports declining motivation among AI users
stories.summary: Silicon Valley psychotherapist Candice Thompson reports that workers are struggling with AI-driven workplace changes. According to Thompson, employees are experiencing lower ambition and motivation as workflows shift. She suggests that leaders should focus on preserving human elements of the workplace and maintaining honest conversations with their staff.

research.title: Conformally Calibrated Adaptive Computation in Neural Operators
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Selecting less computation in a neural operator need not reduce inference time. We study this gap using conformal calibration to choose Fourier modes or channel width per input subject to a fixed error budget. A triangle-inequality. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: CounselTraj: Synthesizing Process-Aware Psychological Counseling Dialogues via Dialogue-Act Trajectory Planning
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: The growing demand for psychological counseling has motivated the development of LLM-based systems that support human counselors, but training such systems requires large-scale, high-quality dialogue data. Authentic counseling transcripts are difficult to collect and share because. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Coverage Governs Accuracy: When to Expand the Lexicon and When to Fall Back in Low-Resource Manchu OCR
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Character-level OCR for low-resource Manchu often produces near-miss spelling errors. Lexicon-constrained decoding can correct such errors with lexical knowledge, but a fixed dictionary cannot cover the many unseen word forms produced by agglutinative word formation. We. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Dreaming Up Authors: Factual Prevalence and LLM Hallucinations in Academic Authorship Attribution
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are widely used for question answering but are prone to hallucinations, yet the underlying causes, particularly the role of factual prevalence in training data, remain underexplored. In this work, we study this. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: DuoCL: Dual-Path Online Continual Learning
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Online continual learning (OCL) requires learning from a data stream whose arrival rate is independent of model training speed. When training cannot keep pace, computationally expensive gradient-based methods update less frequently, limiting adaptation. Analytic methods reduce. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
